newsitem.title: CANADA: Shell Canada, Mobil in asset swap.
newsitem.headline: Shell Canada, Mobil in asset swap.

text.p: Shell Canada Ltd and Mobil Corp. unit Mobil Oil Canada said on Friday they agreed to an asset swap involving properties in Canada's east coast and Alberta.

The companies said Shell Canada would gain half the interest Mobil gained in another property exchange in September, including a nine percent stake in the Sable Offshore Energy Project off the coast of Nova Scotia.

In return, Mobil would acquire a 30 percent interest in Shell's Harmattan East natural gas properties in central Alberta, in a move aimed at strengthening Mobil's position in western Canada, they said.

In the east coast portion of the deal, Shell Canada would acquire nine percent of Mobil's working interest in Sable Island and other interests ranging from two to 23 percent in other offshore acreage on the Scotian Shelf.

The swap would give Shell Canada a total 35 percent pre-development working interest in the Sable project, which is expected to develop about three trillion cubic feet of gas from six fields on the Scotian Shelf.
Mobil will hold a 50 percent pre-development working interest in the project. Other partners include are Imperial Oil Ltd and Nova Scotia Resources Ltd.

The Sable producer partners have filed a development plan application with regulators and have thrown their support behind the Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline Project, which is pursuing the right to transport Sable Island gas to eastern Canada and the U.S. Northeast.
In Alberta, the swap would add 17 million cubic feet of gas and 1,200 barrels gas liquids per day to Mobil's production, it said.
It would also boost its interest in the Harmattan gas plant, Alberta's third-largest processing facility with a capacity of 375 million cubic feet per day.
After the deal, Mobil would be operator of both the Harmattan East and the Harmattan Elkton fields, it said.
